texts.preamble: Ghanshyam Das Karwa vs State Of Telangana on 6 November, 2020
texts.facts: He claims to have secured licence to do the business in jaggery from the Authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and he has been carrying the said business in strict compliance of statutory requirements. He has several godowns to store the goods in which he is carrying on his business. Petitioner alleges Ghanshyam Das Karwa vs State Of Telangana on 6 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70093787/ 1 that on 16.05.2020, he was directed to open the godown in the premises bearing municipal No.14-6-38, Begumbazar, Hyderabad and forcibly took away 288 bags of black jaggery of 30 kgs each, total 8640 kgs, Navsagar powder of 1884.5 kgs and 120 kg Alum. When stock was seized, no information was furnished to the petitioner on reasons for such seizure. On further enquiry, petitioner came to know that said stock was seized in connection with COR.No.70 of 2020 on the file of Prohibition and Excise Station, Deverkonda, based on confessional statement obtained from the accused therein. This writ petition is filed seeking declaration of action of seizure of black jaggery as illegal, arbitrary and contrary to the principles of natural justice and to direct the 5th respondent to release the seized stock. 3. In counter affidavit, respondents contend that petitioner is indulging in manufacture of illicitly distilled liquor (I.D.liquor) and is involved in several crimes. Having come to know that illegal manufacture and sale of I.D.liquor was going on in the house of Nenavath Raju, Uppugandi Thanda, raid was conducted and huge 3 PNRJ WP 16596_2020 quantity of black jaggery, Navasagar powder and Alum were recovered. Based on confession of the accused Nos 1 to 4, raid was conducted in the godwn of petitioner and huge quantity of black jaggery, Navasagar powder and Alum were seized. According to respondents, COR.No.70 of 2020 was registered under Sections 7(A) read with Section 8(e) of A.P. Prohibition Act, 1995 and Section 34 (e) of A.P.Excise Act, 1968 and Section 3 (b) and 4(1) (111) of GUR (Regulation of Excise) Order, 1968 and investigation is pending. It is further case of respondents that from out of seized stock from the godown of the petitioner, samples were collected and sent for chemical examination to the Chemical Examiner, Warangal. The Chemical Examiner has tested the samples and opined that seized jaggery is not useful for human consumption, but it can be used as raw material in manufacturing illicit liquor. 6. In this writ petition, limited grievance of petitioner is against seizure of black jaggery and not releasing the same. The black jaggery was seized based on the confessional statement of accused Nos 1 to 4.
texts.arguments: 4. According to learned counsel for petitioner, jaggery is an agricultural product and there is no prohibition on purchase, transport and sale of black jaggery. On 22.12.2001, the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise issued circular instructions directing the Law Enforcing Authorities not to harass business people, who were doing business in jaggery, as long as purchase is supported by bills and having valid transport documents. According to learned counsel, jaggery was purchased in the State of Maharastra. At the time of purchase, test reports were obtained showing the quality of jaggery as useful for human consumption and manufacturer has issued way bill. Therefore, as it is validly purchased and transported, there is no bar in carrying on business in jaggery. Merely because large quantity of jaggery is stored in the godown of petitioner, based on false confession, respondents could not have seized the jaggery. He further submits that jaggery is perishable item, if it is not released it will perish and petitioner would be subjected to huge financial loss for no fault of him. 4 PNRJ WP 16596_2020 5. Per contra, according to learned Government Pleader, material on record would disclose that petitioner is indulging in manufacture of illicit liquor and the fact that several crimes are registered against him would go to show that he is conniving in manufacturing illicit liquor for a long time. He would submit that it was not necessary that traders should involve in actual manufacturing. If excise officials have reasonable apprehension that huge quantity of jaggery and Alum are stored by a Ghanshyam Das Karwa vs State Of Telangana on 6 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70093787/ 2 person, which is primarily intended to manufacture illicit liquor, it is permissible for the excise officials to seize the stock, so that they can prevent any further manufacturing of illicit liquor which is harmful for human consumption. The crime is already registered and investigation is in progress. He would further submit that as per the Chemical Analysis report, seized black jaggery is not useful for human consumption and therefore, balance of convenience is not in favour of petitioner to release the seized stock before investigation is completed and before confiscation proceedings are concluded. In support of his contention, learned Government Pleader placed reliance on decision of Full Bench of this Court in Ganesh Traders (Kirana and General Merchants), Dhermapuri, Karimnagar District v. District Collector, Karimnagar1 and decision of learned Judge of Common High Court in W.P.No.9471 of 2018. On the scope of power of excise officials seizing black jaggery whenever they suspect that it is being used to produce illicit liquor need not detain this Court further having regard to the conclusions recorded in the majority opinion of the Full Bench in Ganesh Traders. Paragraph No.52 reads as under: "52. (a) The provisions of the A. P. Excise Act including Sections 13(f) and 34(e) should be interpreted with reference to the objects of the Act and penal provisions dealing with excise offences should also receive broader interpretation having regard to the fact that the Excise Act is intended to achieve partially the objective of Article 47 of the Constitution of India; (b) Having regard to the provisions of Sections 13, 34 and 53 and 55 of the Excise Act, we must hold that if Commissioner, Collector, Police Officer or Excise Officer "has reason to believe" that black jaggery (material) is likely to be used for manufacture of Ghanshyam Das Karwa vs State Of Telangana on 6 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70093787/ 3 ID liquor the same can be seized and persons can be arrested and subject to facts and circumstances of each case including any report of the chemical examiner a charge sheet can be filed under Section 34(e) of the Excise Act. (d) As held by the Supreme Court in NASU SHEIKKS case (supra) if the F.I.R. shows the ingredients of offence under Section 34(e) read with Section 13(f) of the Excise Act, a person cannot be heard to say in High Court that he is carrying on business or transporting black jaggery either because he is an agriculturist or businessman.
